newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper seen lower, aluminium higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper seen lower, aluminium higher.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are likely to come under pressure on Monday and may test support at $2,285 a tonne on the back of rising London Metal Exchange (LME) inventories, traders and chartists said.
Uptrending charts and physical demand may see aluminium move towards $1,775 resistance, though several market operators are expecting flurries of profit-taking.

COPPER - Rising LME stocks and a downtrending chart close on Friday is expected to pressure copper lower, possibly towards the July 30 and 31 lows of $2,285 a tonne, traders and analysts said on Monday.
"Another softish close which with the moving day averages trending lower, in particular the 10-day, the bias remains to the downside," LME brokers Brandeis said.
Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading said that if $2,285 breaks, falls to $2,266 and $2,250 could be seen.
Last week copper stocks held in LME warehouses rose by 24,725 tonnes to 234,950 tonnes.
Several traders are expecting the pace of increases to continue this week.
"Sentiment continues to be weighed upon by the prospect of a looming market surplus and rising stocks," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.
On the upside Squires said he favoured selling rallies towards $2,400.
Creates pegged resistance at a fanline at $2,325, followed by $2,410.
At 0700 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,300/2,305, unchanged from Friday's late London close.
ALUMINIUM - Seen moving higher towards initial resistance at $1,750 and then $1,775 a tonne. Creates of AMT said that aluminium had a bullish close on Friday "indicating further to go on the upside."
But traders and analysts said that the gains seen in aluminium recently may find profit-taking and liquidation as some chart signals look over-extended.
"Above $1,750 progress is likely to be slow with an area of congestion towards $1,825 evident, whilst the market still remains seriously overbought," brokers Brandeis said.
"We are expecting a corrective pull back of sorts to emerge," Squires of Wolff said.
But Squires expected downside movements to provide buying opportunities with support light at $1,700 and then strong between $1,650/65.
"The short term technical indicators are looking fairly overcooked," Squires commented.
At 0700 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,738/43, against $1,738/40.
